paragraphs: R' Simlai de-Veroyra: Midrash Kohelet, at “I know that whatever God does.” Mattenot Kehunah explains it as a place-name. The midrash's wording is: Resh Lakish said, “It is written, ‘All the word that I command you … you shall not add to it or subtract from it.’ But the righteous add to it and do not subtract.” R' Yose bar R' Hanina said, “From here we learn that a private altar is permitted only through a prophet; yet Eliyahu stood and offered on the summit of Carmel.” R' Simlai de-Veroyra said, “He told him: ‘At Your word I have done all these things’”: I Kings 18. In this matter in Midrash Rabbah, Aharei Mot, chapter 22: “Yet Eliyahu stood and offered at a time when private altars were forbidden.” R' Simlai said, “The Holy One, blessed be He, told him,” as it says, “At Your word I have done.” It occurred to my mind and thought to explain and emend it to “R' Simlai: dibburi”—that is, by the divine utterance, as it says, “At Your word I have done”—because I did not find R' Simlai de-Veroyra anywhere in the Talmud or midrash. I labored and found in Jerusalem Ta'anit, chapter 2, halakhah 8: “R' Simlai: dibbira, He told him; at Your word I have done.” There, in Megillah, chapter 1, halakhah 13: “R' Simlai: dibbira, He told him; at Your word I have done.” The commentator there explains dibbira as “by the utterance of the Divine Presence.” End of quotation; and it pleased me. Nevertheless, I am uncertain about deciding the matter. You, master and scholar, see what to bring near, what will be pleasing to your palate.
